summary_paragraph: A female patient with a complex medical history including end-stage renal disease, antiphospholipid syndrome, systemic lupus erythematosus, and seizure disorder was admitted for abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, and weakness. Imaging revealed significant fecal loading and findings consistent with mild ileus likely due to gastroenteritis and poor oral intake. She was treated with an aggressive bowel regimen and hemodialysis, which resolved her hyperkalemia and improved her symptoms. Her shoulder pain was attributed to bursitis and managed conservatively. She remained stable throughout the admission, with improvement in abdominal symptoms and normalization of electrolytes. She was discharged home with instructions to continue laxatives, resume her regular medications including macitentan, and follow up with her specialists.
